reading.value: The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation, checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its inputs and states exactly what its checks establish. This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence. The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.
reading.roleRequirement: Explain the need for a fixed comparison point when extending an existing tokenizer/decoder pipeline. State the limitation of unidentified changing inputs before naming identity machinery; do not ask the learner a question or request a prediction.

reading.value: What the reference actually does The fixture assigns 8 documents to training, 2 to validation and 2 to test. The decoder has 1188 learned scalar parameters and context capacity 4 tokens. Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform 32 updates on full batches of 16 windows, with 4 valid targets per window. Therefore, each schedule consumes 32\cdot16\cdot4=2048 valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: 4096 targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated tokens are separate quantities. The report’s independent_schedules field counts two separately executed copies of the same schedule from training seed 39, not statistically independent seed samples. The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same 1744 overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are approximately 3.866087547 and 3.981342714 nats per slot, respectively. This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization. There are only 442 within-document transition occurrences in those test documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so 1744 is not a count of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once, using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or perplexity under that policy. The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed At probe, encoded as token IDs [67,118]. Cached and complete-prefix generation agree on token IDs [260,34,34]: Cyrillic т followed by two spaces. Agreement checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful language quality.

reading.value: The solution: identify inputs, then interpret evidence R_{\mathrm{ref}}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{config}_{1188}\Vert\mathrm{fixture}\Vert\mathrm{source\_revision})
reading.roleRequirement: Introduce the reference input-identity equation in the solution's reading order. The immediately following symbol/settings unit explains its inputs and canonical encoding; this introductory equation unit need not duplicate that explanation.

reading.value: The identity’s symbols and fixed settings R_{\mathrm{ref}} is a 256-bit digest, displayed as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Its three named inputs are: \mathrm{config}_{1188}: a canonical record of eighteen tiny-run settings, together with the invariant that the decoder has 1188 parameters. \mathrm{fixture}: a canonical record of SHA-256 digests of the exact corpus bytes and exact split-manifest bytes. Even a byte change that leaves parsed JSON meaning unchanged creates a different input identity. \mathrm{source\_revision}: a verified source identity combining a baseline revision with the exact forty course-owned scalar-reference source files. Here \Vert means composition into the shared identity format’s named, canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another. That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes. The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context capacity of four; one attention head and one block; stride one; training and evaluation batch sizes of sixteen and one hundred twenty-eight; thirty-two updates; learning rate 0.04; gradient-norm cap 1; training seed 39; generation seed 38; bigram smoothing 1; generation temperature 0.8; top-k four; and three generated tokens. The identity records floating-point settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text. Bind configuration, exact fixture bytes and verified scalar-reference source to one input identity. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-input-identity /// Bind every tiny-config field, including exact represented floating values. /// The count is the reference decoder's required 1,188-parameter invariant. pub fn tiny_config_identity() -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let fields = [ ("parameters", "1188".to_owned()), ("bpe_merges", config.bpe_merges().to_string()), ("model_width", config.model_width().to_string()), ("heads", config.heads().to_string()), ( "feed_forward_width", config.feed_forward_width().to_string(), ), ("layers", config.layers().to_string()), ("context_length", config.context_length().to_string()), ("window_stride", config.window_stride().to_string()), ("update_batch_size", config.update_batch_size().to_string()), ( "evaluation_batch_size", config.evaluation_batch_size().to_string(), ), ("updates", config.updates().to_string()), ( "learning_rate_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.learning_rate().to_bits()), ), ( "max_gradient_norm_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.max_gradient_norm().to_bits()), ), ("seed", config.seed().to_string()), ("generation_seed", config.generation_seed().to_string()), ( "bigram_alpha_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.bigram_alpha().to_bits()), ), ( "generation_temperature_f64_bits", format!("{:016x}", config.generation_temperature().to_bits()), ), ("generation_top_k", config.generation_top_k().to_string()), ("generation_tokens", config.generation_tokens().to_string()), ]; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_config", fields.iter().map(|(key, value)| (*key, value.as_str())), ) } /// Pure identity construction, also usable by mutation tests without training. /// An identity by itself does not admit alternate inputs to the reference run. pub fn reference_input_identity( config: &ArtifactIdentity, corpus: &[u8], splits: &[u8], source: &ArtifactIdentity, ) -> Result<ArtifactIdentity, IdentityError> { let corpus_digest = sha256(corpus); let splits_digest = sha256(splits); let fixture = ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_fixture", [ ("corpus_sha256", corpus_digest.as_hex()), ("splits_sha256", splits_digest.as_hex()), ], )?; let config_bytes = canonical_string(config)?; let fixture_bytes = canonical_string(&fixture)?; let source_bytes = canonical_string(source)?; ArtifactIdentity::new( "scalar_reference_run", [ ("config_1188", config_bytes.as_str()), ("fixture", fixture_bytes.as_str()), ("source_revision", source_bytes.as_str()), ], ) } The example verifies its compiled reference-source evidence first. It then rejects changed corpus or split bytes before training or checkpoint work. Only accepted fixed inputs reach the existing pipeline. The wrapper calls that pipeline once; the pipeline itself performs primary training and replay. Reject changed fixtures, run the unchanged scalar pipeline and retain only its checked observation. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#reference-handoff /// Refuse changed fixtures before model/checkpoint work, then call the existing /// capstone once. That call already includes primary training and full replay. pub fn run_reference_handoff( corpus_source: &str, split_source: &str, checkpoint_path: impl AsRef<Path>, source: &ReferenceSourceProof, ) -> Result<ReferenceHandoffTrace, ReferenceHandoffError> { if sha256(corpus_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != CORPUS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("corpus")); } if sha256(split_source.as_bytes()).as_hex() != SPLITS_SHA256 { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::FixtureMismatch("split manifest")); } // Safe callers obtain this opaque proof only through the foundation's // approved-manifest/compiled-census verification, not a revision string. let identity = reference_input_identity( &tiny_config_identity()?, corpus_source.as_bytes(), split_source.as_bytes(), source.identity(), )?; let digest = identity.digest()?; let observation = run_capstone( corpus_source, split_source, checkpoint_path, CapstoneConfig::tiny(), )?; let evaluation = observation.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = observation.checkpoint(); if observation.training().parameter_count() != 1188 || observation.training().optimizer_step() != 32 || !observation.training().replay_bitwise() || evaluation.window_count() != 436 || evaluation.window_target_slot_count() != 1744 || evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count() != 442 || !evaluation.decoder().mean_nll().is_finite() || !evaluation.bigram().mean_nll().is_finite() || !checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip() || !checkpoint.model_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact() || !checkpoint.tokenizer_exact() || !checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise() || !observation.generation().tokens_exact() || !observation.generation().decisions_bitwise() || !observation.generation().rng_state_exact() { return Err(ReferenceHandoffError::Invariant( "scalar reference handoff evidence changed", )); } Ok(ReferenceHandoffTrace { identity, digest, source_revision: source.source_revision().to_owned(), observation, }) } What matching identities do not prove A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit. The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match. The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs. Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption. This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.

reading.value: History: reporting conditions and measuring variation A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked. Model Cards for Model Reporting was presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself proof of quality. Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting scope and measuring variation answer different questions. In Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping, published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder. Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims. The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean NLL with this expression gives a number: trace .observation() .final_evaluation() .decoder() .mean_nll() trace.report() also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed sweep. Report the same scalar observation with its metric unit, input identity and explicit capability limits. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/lib.rs#scope-bearing-report /// Read structured evidence from this one observation; never parse stdout /// or run another model to produce either reporting projection. pub fn report(&self) -> Result<String, ReferenceHandoffError> { let run = &self.observation; let evaluation = run.final_evaluation(); let checkpoint = run.checkpoint(); let generation = run.generation(); let config = CapstoneConfig::tiny(); let targets_per_schedule = config.updates() * config.update_batch_size() * config.context_length(); let record = serde_json::json!({ "schema_version": 1, "chapter": "40-reference-core-handoff", "reference_identity": self.digest.as_hex(), "source_revision": self.source_revision, "scope": "scalar-reference-fixed-fixture-regression", "documents": { "train": run.partitions().train_document_ids().len(), "validation": run.partitions().validation_document_ids().len(), "test": run.partitions().test_document_ids().len() }, "model": { "parameters": run.training().parameter_count(), "context_tokens": config.context_length() }, "training": { "target_count_basis": "derived-from-frozen-full-batch-schedules", "updates_per_schedule": config.updates(), "independent_schedules": 2, "valid_targets_per_schedule": targets_per_schedule, "valid_targets_primary_plus_replay": 2 * targets_per_schedule, "selected_step": run.training().selected_step(), "within_invocation_replay_bitwise": run.training().replay_bitwise() }, "evaluation": { "unit": "overlapping-window-target-slot", "windows": evaluation.window_count(), "window_target_slots": evaluation.window_target_slot_count(), "document_transition_occurrences": evaluation.document_transition_occurrence_count(), "transition_multiplicity_counts": evaluation.transition_multiplicity_counts(), "decoder_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.decoder().mean_nll(), "bigram_mean_nll_nats_per_slot": evaluation.bigram().mean_nll(), "once_per_transition_metric_reported": false, "independent_generalization_estimate": false }, "checkpoint": { "bytes_roundtrip": checkpoint.bytes_roundtrip(), "model_bits_exact": checkpoint.model_bits_exact(), "optimizer_bits_exact": checkpoint.optimizer_bits_exact(), "tokenizer_exact": checkpoint.tokenizer_exact(), "logit_probe_text": checkpoint.logit_probe_text(), "logit_probe_ids": checkpoint.logit_probe_ids(), "probe_logits_bitwise": checkpoint.prompt_logits_bitwise(), "complete_job_resume_established": false }, "generation": { "prompt": generation.prompt_text(), "token_ids": generation.generated_ids(), "decoded_text": generation.decoded_text(), "cached_reference_tokens_exact": generation.tokens_exact(), "cached_reference_decisions_bitwise": generation.decisions_bitwise(), "cached_reference_rng_exact": generation.rng_state_exact(), "useful_language_quality_established": false }, "laptop_throughput_measured": false, "successor_chapter": SUCCESSOR_CHAPTER }); let mut text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&record) .map_err(|_| ReferenceHandoffError::Serialization)?; text.push('\n'); Ok(text) } Repeating seed 39 checks repeatability under fixed conditions. It does not estimate variability across seeds. Those are complementary checks, not interchangeable evidence.
reading.roleRequirement: State the two primary sources' supported reporting and variation claims with correct titles and chronology; separate same-seed replay from seed variability and compare the scalar getter with the scope-bearing report from one observation,without pretending to execute historical models.

reading.value: Run the reference without changing its inputs The example obtains verified source evidence and owns its temporary checkpoint location. Its report comes directly from the checked scalar observation, not from parsing a previous human-readable report. Verify the reference source, use an owned temporary checkpoint and print the scope-bearing report. rust/demos/ch40-reference-core-handoff/src/main.rs#reference-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let source = verify_compiled_reference_source()?; let checkpoint = OwnedCheckpoint::new()?; let trace = run_reference_handoff(CORPUS, SPLITS, &checkpoint.file, &source)?; print!("{}", trace.report()?); Ok(()) }
reading.roleRequirement: Explain and show the actual demo ordering: obtain verified source,own the temporary checkpoint,invoke the unchanged pipeline and print its structured scope-bearing report. Do not hide the pipeline's primary-plus-replay schedules.

reading.value: Keep the three evidence layers separate The digest identifies the fixed inputs. The counts and generated token IDs describe checked behavior on those inputs. The final card keeps future quality, job-resumption and hardware claims outside the reference’s evidence boundary. A reference identity is not a capability certificate The configuration, exact corpus and split bytes, and verified scalar-reference source determine the input identity. Separate checks observe replay, fixed-window evaluation, reload and cached generation. Neither the identity nor those checks establishes useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput. Identify the fixed inputs SHA-256 identity of the fixed input record cd06104ff61dc8a0c6cbe6e842847952343050eb4942c79aa1d17e8d0d0bb648 Learned scalar parameters 1188 Read the checked reference behavior Overlapping test-window target slots 1744 Within-document transition occurrences 442 Generated token IDs [260,34,34] Keep unmeasured capabilities separate Not established: useful language quality, complete job resumption or laptop throughput.
reading.roleRequirement: Explain the relationship among identified inputs,checked behavior and unmeasured capabilities,using the actual trace-backed figure and explicit descriptions rather than position or color alone.

reading.value: Optional practice: inspect the boundary Run the example and inspect its report: cargo run --quiet --locked -p ch40-reference-core-handoff Find the identity, target-count basis and metric unit in the output. Explain why a digest alone would not replace the replay and reload checks. Run the demo’s tests. Identify the tests that change configuration, corpus, split bytes and source identity without training. Explain why constructing an identity for changed inputs does not admit them to the fixed reference run. Explain why a successful checkpoint round trip cannot justify the statement “the complete training job can resume,” and why 1744 must not be labeled “distinct test transitions.” Answers: input identity, evidence scope and repeated target slots The digest binds inputs; replay and reload compare actual behavior. Neither kind of evidence substitutes for the other. The target-count basis explicitly derives 2048 targets per schedule and 4096 for primary plus replay. The reported mean NLL uses nats per overlapping window-target slot. The pure mutation tests construct different identities without calling the pipeline. The runner separately requires the exact accepted corpus and split bytes, so an identity is not an admission permit. The checkpoint check covers persisted model, optimizer and tokenizer state plus a fixed logit probe, not every whole-job continuation dependency. The 1744 denominator counts overlapping window-target slots; the underlying documents contain 442 transition occurrences.
reading.roleRequirement: Offer optional inspection,reproduction and explanation tasks with one substantive answer per task. Preserve identity-versus-evidence,construction-versus-admission,checkpoint-versus-job andslots-versus-transitions boundaries; no prediction requests.
